ref: verifier prompt § Grouping refinements + eval/prompts/tilize.txt § Refinement queue
what: The verifier prompt hard-targets "3-5 refinements total. Not 8. Not 12.", but the op prompt for tilize prescribes its own 16-phase queue (A0-A7, P1-P5, T1-T2) with an explicit adoption order (A0->A1->P1->P2->A2->...), and TARGET-SUPPORTED leaves 15 axes with missing values. The two cannot both be honoured: even after aggressive bundling the honest queue is 6 generality entries, and the mandated 2:1 perf cadence plus the run-closing Mode-D audit pushes it to 10. I also had to silently arbitrate an ordering conflict (op prompt puts padding before sharding; verifier prompt says hardest-first, which is sharding first).
suggest: State that the 3-5 target is a heuristic that yields to (a) an op prompt that prescribes its own phase list and (b) the axis-coverage requirement, and say which prompt wins on ORDERING when an op prompt fixes an adoption order that contradicts hardest-first (my read: a true dependency in the op prompt wins, otherwise hardest-first).

what: The Output Summary table lists verifier_report.json as a deliverable to keep as an artifact, and the task says "Commit everything when done". The file this op produced is 1.2 MB and the repo pre-commit hook check-large-files rejects anything >500 KB, so the commit failed twice (once on size, once on the end-of-file-fixer rewriting the JSON) before I split it into a compacted verifier_report.summary.json. Any op with a large golden matrix hits this.
suggest: Say explicitly that verifier_report.json stays in <results_dir> and is NOT committed (or that a compacted summary is committed instead), so the agent does not discover the 500 KB pre-commit limit at commit time.
